newsitem.title: USA: ComEd, NRC to meet this week on nuclear plants.
newsitem.headline: ComEd, NRC to meet this week on nuclear plants.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Tuesday it will meet with representatives of Unicom Corp's Commonwealth Edison Co unit on Friday to discuss the utility's plan to address performance issues at six nuclear power plants in Illinois.
In January, the NRC placed ComEd's Zion and LaSalle stations on its list of plants with declining performance. ComEd's Dresden plant has been on the watch list since 1992.
Last month, ComEd responded in a 60-page letter to an NRC request for information on how it will address the regulatory agency's concerns.

The March 28 letter contained more than 200 specific site actions aimed at upgrading engineering and technical support throughout the nuclear plant division. It also focused on improved oversight, a standardization of procedures and heightened enforcement of performance standards.
The utility also boosted its budget for expenditures at the nuclear operations by 11 percent to $1.028 billion.

Meanwhile, ComEd last week announced it will close the Zion facility much earlier than its licensed life of 2013 and most likely before 2005. The company decided not to spend the $400 million it would take to replace Zion's steam generators.

The NRC said the meeting this Friday is expected to outline information on why the NRC should have confidence in ComEd to continue operating the nuclear stations while trying to improve performance. It will also address what steps will be taken if the performance criteria Com Ed has established or plans to establish are not met.
Unicom shares were up 1/8 Tuesday at 19-3/8.
